chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When the woman is divorced, then her husband dies while she is in her waiting period (iddah) from him, she has not become prohibited to him; therefore, she inherits him and he inherits her as long as she is in the blood (flow) of her second menstruation from the first two divorces. If he divorces her for the third time, she does not inherit anything from her husband, nor does he inherit from her.

key_terms.عِدَّةٍ: Waiting period (Iddah) after divorce or death

ai.seo_question: Does a divorced woman inherit from her husband if he dies during her waiting period?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the specific duration of the 'iddah' for inheritance purposes in cases of revocable divorce, linking the right to inherit to the woman's second menstrual cycle after the initial declaration. It highlights the legal distinction between revocable and final divorces, noting that upon the third divorce, the marital bond is severed completely, thereby extinguishing mutual inheritance rights. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the continuity of the marital link during the waiting period as the basis for financial entitlements.
